questions.q: In Salesforce terms, what is an object?
options: A container that defines a type of data, like a table
A single saved row of data
A single column on a record
A button on a record page
questions.explain: An object is the table-like container for one kind of data, such as Account or Contact. Fields are its columns, records are its rows.

questions.q: Using the spreadsheet analogy, what does a field correspond to?
options: The whole spreadsheet
A single row
A column header
A saved file
questions.explain: A field is one property every record of that object has — the equivalent of a column header in a spreadsheet.

options: The definition of an object's fields
One saved, real instance of an object
A relationship between two objects
A report built from an object
questions.explain: A record is one row of real, saved data — one actual company, person, or property, not the definition of the object itself.

questions.q: Two records belong to the same object. What must be true?
options: They must have identical field values
They must have been created on the same day
They must be owned by the same user
They must share the same set of fields, though values can differ
questions.explain: Belonging to the same object means sharing the same defined fields (shape). The actual values in those fields are free to differ record to record.

questions.q: A spreadsheet of property listings is moved into Salesforce as a Property object. What do the spreadsheet's column headers become?
options: Records
Reports
Fields
Page layouts
questions.explain: Column headers like Price or Bedrooms map onto fields on the object; each spreadsheet row becomes a record of that object.
